name: 38 cm/52 SK C/34
_barrelLengthComment: Barrel length in calibres, the standard naval convention: a 16"/50 has a barrel 50 x 16 inches long. Longer barrels give higher muzzle velocity for the same charge.
_elevationComment: Maximum elevation sets maximum range as firmly as muzzle velocity does. Bismarck's 30 degree limit is why her very high velocity guns still out-range nobody.
_muzzleHeightComment: Height of the gun axis above the waterline. It matters more than it looks: a gun firing at zero elevation from sea level would put its shell in the water immediately, so this is what gives flat trajectories a usable short range. Capital ship main batteries sit high; destroyer guns are close to the water.
_dispersionComment: One standard deviation, as a percentage of range. Range dispersion is always much larger than deflection: a salvo lands in a long thin ellipse along the line of fire, which is why straddles are common and hits are not.
notes: Very high muzzle velocity and a fast-firing mounting; the 30 degree elevation limit costs it range against later designs.
